value.decision: Theo 2026-09-28: 'should we be deprecating the old stuff and removing it? this project is greenfield, we can delete whatever'. Root answer: yes. Facts: no roster crate depends on ts_goport, but ts_goport depends on 12 legacy crates, including ts_compiler, which pulls in ts_checker (1.32M lines), ts_binder and ts_printer. Plan: workflow legacy-removal-audit (read only) maps each use and the acceptance pipeline, then staged removal: cut goport's legacy dependencies; retire the legacy cargo roster (the 6,055 and 6,330 names test the old stack) and make goport's own tests and gate items the protected baseline; delete the legacy crates and tools. The acceptance-rule change is made under this message from Theo and is recorded in acceptanceRuleChanges when it lands. Historical evidence stays unchanged. R131 finishes under the current rules.

Theo 2026-09-28, direct approval: 'i approve any rule changes that allow removing the legacy code'. This approves the acceptance-rule changes needed to retire the legacy cargo roster (ts_checker, ts_compiler, ts_fixture stages, the current-source corpus, the 6,055 and 6,330 legacy names) and to delete the legacy crates, tools and scripts. Root will write the replacement rule (goport's own tests per name and the gate items become the protected set; no lost pass allowed) into docs/typechecker-accountability.md and AGENTS.md and record it in acceptanceRuleChanges citing this approval. Historical evidence and records stay unchanged. The independent reviewer checks that the new protected set is complete.

acceptanceRuleChanges.scope: Every batch opened after R132 (open_revision.py --new-batch sets protectedSet goport). The protected set is goport's own evidence: every goport test name (docs/goport-protected/tests-r131.json.gz, then the results of the last accepted goport revision), every gate item against the last accepted gate manifest, every gate run of the source (gateRuns; a failed run needs a flake note for each regression), the bound Query and Hono runs, the LSP oracle (6 batteries) and API oracle (10 batteries) per request, np-suite, quality and both verdicts. After a legacy batch the test, API and np-suite bases are the R131 runs (tests-r131.json.gz, api-r131, np-r131). While the defect editor-long-growth is open, editor/query-core/long and editor/hono/long can FAIL only on growth, at most the fixed caps in gate-compare.py LONG_CAP (query-core 1.58, hono 1.28 MiB/edit). A cap only goes down; only Theo can raise one. A lost, absent or unrun base pass is STOP; new passes do not compensate. Name maps only for pin bumps and moved or replaced tests, with Go evidence at the new pin, checked by the reviewer. The legacy cargo roster (6,055 and 6,330 names), the roster drive, the current-source corpus and the roster carry-forward are retired for new batches; R132 (batch port-18, opened under them before this rule) is the last revision under them. For goport batches this replaces the 'Protected cargo roster' clause of pin-bump-batch. Old batches keep their rules. Root must not widen it. Gate tools: every tool hash in the gate manifest (oracle, Go dumper, gate.sh, allow list, stage scripts, saved Go output families in oracleCaches) must equal the base run's, unless batch.gateToolChanges lists the exact change for the reviewer. Evidence builds: only the candidate checkout builds in the shared candidate target.

value.result: Legacy removal stage 1 merged into main (goport-legacy1 a6bf5137f; reviewer PASS after 3 rounds, auditor PASS). The protected set is goport's own evidence (docs/goport-protected/tests-r131.json.gz sha256 d1b90114690033ea0d3450182b7340c7f87df27d7e3c45af07192506a2476b7a; api-r131; np-r131; gate items and gate tools against the base run; bound Query and Hono; LSP and API oracles; quality; both verdicts). The legacy cargo roster, drive, corpus and carry-forward are retired; R132 was the last legacy revision. Rule entry goport-protected-set recorded in acceptanceRuleChanges. archive-rules moved the port-13 to port-17 rules to history.

value.hypothesis: No goport output uses the legacy loader or the legacy crate stack. Deleting them keeps goport and tsgo stdout, exit codes and emitted files byte-equal to R132, keeps every protected goport test name, takes the None-arm checks out of the hot paths, and makes a clean release build about 2.7x faster (208 s to 76 s on dbook-lan).
value.change: R132 + goport-legacy2 3a94ce888. Stage 2: remove the GOPORT_FRONTEND=legacy loader and every legacy fallback in program.rs, options.rs, core.rs, ast/*, go_frontend.rs, execute/tsc/diagnostics.rs and modulespecifiers/host.rs; delete ast/jsdoc.rs, ast/parser_flags.rs, ast/go_view.rs and program/verify_options.rs; keep the 2 alias resolver arms; goport no longer depends on ts_compiler, ts_parser, ts_diagnostic_writer, ts_module, ts_options or ts_vfs; lib blobs regenerated. Stage 3: delete the 23 legacy crates (keep crates/ts_bundled/libs/), tools/ts_fixture, tools/ts_compare, the legacy scripts, docs and dead test data. Workspace: ts_goport, goport_util, goport_lsproto, the 6 kept crates (ts_ast, ts_core, ts_diagnostics, ts_jsnum, ts_path, ts_scanner) and the 2 codegen tools.

The protected set is goport's own evidence: every goport test name (docs/goport-protected/tests-r131.json.gz, then the results of the last accepted goport revision), every gate item against the last accepted gate manifest, every gate run of the source (gateRuns; a failed run needs a flake note for each regression), the bound Query and Hono runs, the LSP oracle (6 batteries) and API oracle (10 batteries) per request, np-suite, quality and both verdicts. After a legacy batch the test, API and np-suite bases are the R131 runs (tests-r131.json.gz, api-r131, np-r131). While the defect editor-long-growth is open, editor/query-core/long and editor/hono/long can FAIL only on growth, at most the fixed caps in gate-compare.py LONG_CAP (query-core 1.58, hono 1.28 MiB/edit). A cap only goes down; only Theo can raise one. A lost, absent or unrun base pass is STOP; new passes do not compensate. Name maps only for pin bumps and moved or replaced tests, with Go evidence at the new pin, checked by the reviewer. The legacy cargo roster (6,055 and 6,330 names), the roster drive, the current-source corpus and the roster carry-forward are retired for new batches; R132 (batch port-18, opened under them before this rule) is the last revision under them. For goport batches this replaces the 'Protected cargo roster' clause of pin-bump-batch. Old batches keep their rules. Root must not widen it. Gate tools: every tool hash in the gate manifest (oracle, Go dumper, gate.sh, allow list, stage scripts, saved Go output families in oracleCaches) must equal the base run's, unless batch.gateToolChanges lists the exact change for the reviewer. Evidence builds: only the candidate checkout builds in the shared candidate target.

value.change: R134 + goport-perf14 07f0bd5aa (main fb5d6fb31 merged into 021655609, no conflicts), 35 files in crates/ts_goport/src/checker/. Round 1 (375a69f92): resolve_name, get_is_deferred_context and is_self_reference_location read each scope kind once; flow helpers borrow antecedent slices and take the FlowNode already read; is_matching_reference reads the target kind once; mark_node_assignments_worker calls itself directly; is_block_scoped_name_declared_before_use gets the container after the early returns. Round 2 (28627fbe0): an is_matching_reference memo of the last identifier source (is_this_in_type_query, resolved symbol, export symbol), made invalid by a merge_version counter that merge_symbol and record_merged_symbol increase; an early false for a property-access source against a target that is not an access expression. Round 3 (021655609): NodeSlice read in place in 26 files; check_source_elements, check_type_parameters, check_type_parameters_not_referenced and append_type_parameters take slices or iterators; get_effective_property_name_for_property_name_node returns Cow<'static, str>; infer_from_properties and is_from_inference_blocked_source skip the scan when the skip-direct-inference set is empty.

Against it every direct -p cell is 2x or more on THP=madvise hosts; under 2x: effect emit fragmented 1.81 to 1.85, --singleThreaded query 1.82 to 1.86, tsc -b chains 1.2 to 2.0 (a wide 12-project -b is 0.61), watch rebuild 1.3 to 1.7, --version 0.84, through the npm Node launcher 1.65 to 1.85 on query (+22.5 ms both sides; 212 of 292 wide configs under 2x). Against Go at bump B pin (1.09x to 1.40x faster than Go at main's pin) and the 7.1 nightly: effect check 1.49 to 1.67. Compatibility at the pin: 0 test failures, gate 3,951 MATCH and 4 Go-nondeterminism ALLOWED; real gaps: std sort panic class (48 sites; 8 vscode requests fail), .tsbuildinfo package.json lists under threads, bundled:/// lib paths (noembed missing), version 7.1.0-dev, ulimit -v panic (1 GiB stacks), 11 unported sites. typescript-go is archived; upstream is microsoft/TypeScript tsc/ (bump C tooling needed). Platforms: linux-x64 glibc only; a 114-line cfg patch makes cargo check pass for darwin, windows and musl; watchers, pipes and arm64 constants missing. Editor: growth and edit latency not at 2x (effect 0.8x, vscode slower). Root decisions: target upstream (7.1) through pin bumps while keeping a build-time version for 7.0.x identity; wave 1 (gaps-wave1: sortfix, pjcache, stacks, platforms1, identity, perfB analysis) started. value.hypothesis: When a run gets 4 KiB pages (fragmented memory, THP off or never), a worker copy of tsgo does the work and sends its exit code over a pipe once its output is written, so tsgo exits without waiting about 50 ms for its memory to unmap. Effect emit on fragmented memory gets 54 to 56 ms faster (32 CPUs 1.79x to 1.92x, 16 CPUs 1.86x to 1.99x of Go). Runs on clean memory keep the R136 path. Every output stays byte-equal, and the exit code or death signal a caller sees is the same as without a worker.
value.change: R136 + goport-perf16 23c474d4d: thp_guard returns whether the run gets huge pages; bin/tsgo.rs launch starts a worker copy when it does not (GOPORT_LAUNCH=0 off, 1 on; not for --lsp, --api or watch). The worker sets a parent-death SIGKILL, checks getppid against GOPORT_LAUNCHER_PID, points stdout and stderr at /dev/null and writes its exit code to the pipe at exit. The launcher sends SIGINT and SIGTERM on to the worker and, when the worker dies by a signal, dies by the same signal (signal-hook emulate_default_handler). rustix gets the stdio feature. build-release.sh and build-pgo.sh export GOPORT_LAUNCH=0 for the training runs.

value.hypothesis: Five gap audit fixes and the R137 worker hardening close gaps with Go, and emit and check output on query, hono, zod and effect stays byte-equal to R137. (1) pjcache: multi-threaded -p --incremental writes Go's packageJsons and missingPackageJsons lists, the same in each run. (2) sortfix: each ported Go sort site uses the Go sort that it ports, so a comparator that is not a total order (compareSymbols) cannot panic, and the vscode imports codeAction and completion panics stop. (3) stacks: thread stacks and glibc arenas follow RLIMIT_AS and RLIMIT_DATA, so query check and emit give Go's output under ulimit -v 2G to 8G, where R137 exits 70; with no limit nothing changes. (4) identity: a build-time version and a port of Go's noembed build let a release build match shipped tsc 7.0.2, and the default build is unchanged. (5) platforms1: cfg gates let ts_goport pass cargo check for darwin, windows and arm64 Linux, and fswatch uses the target's open flags on arm64 Linux. (6) R137 follow-up 3: a tsgo is a worker only when its parent is the launcher, so a tsgo started from a worker runs as a plain tsgo and is not killed. R137 follow-up 2: the tsgo CLI audit gives the same results at GOPORT_LAUNCH=1, GOPORT_LAUNCH=0 and Go.
value.change: main 3717d4d9a (R137) + goport-gaps1-int d14ba56e3: merges of goport-pjcache 2025dbc7b, goport-sortfix 5a4b95150, goport-stacks 8ea06f135, goport-identity 9005711bd and goport-platforms1 40a17f2e3, then 3 commits. pjcache: each SharedResolutionCache answer carries the package.json lookups of its resolution (SharedResolution, PackageJsonLookup), and Resolver::package_json_cache_entries adds the lookups of the answers that the loader took (incremental and -b runs only). sortfix: 36 std sort calls and 1 hand-written insertion sort change to gostd::slices sorts (21 sort_func, 6 sort_slice, 10 sort_stable_func), each with its Go reference; sorts of plain ordered values and port-only sorts on Ord keys stay on std; PORTING.md says never to use a std sort with a comparator; 2 gostd::slices unit tests. stacks: new gostd::stack::max_stack_size (1 GiB with no limit, else 1/64 of the smaller of RLIMIT_AS and RLIMIT_DATA, clamped to 8 MiB..1 GiB, from rustix getrlimit, computed once) at all 19 stack sites; ThreadBudget::glibc_tunables gives arena_max=1 under an address space or data limit, and set_malloc_tunables sets only the variables that the caller did not set and execs only when one is left; 1 unit test. identity: core.rs VERSION reads option_env!(GOPORT_BUILD_VERSION), default 7.1.0-dev, and modulespecifiers uses it; Go embed.go moves to frontend/bundled/embed.rs and the new noembed.rs ports noembed.go behind cargo feature noembed; the parse snapshot key hashes the lib base name; build-release.sh adds noembed when RELEASE_VERSION is set; new scripts/copy-libs.sh. platforms1: nix and name-to-handle-at become Linux-only dependencies and jemalloc is not built for msvc; fswatch unix.rs and walkdir_unix.rs are Linux only, Errno moves to fswatch/syscall.rs, and the O_* and IN_* flags come from rustix for the target with compile-time checks against the Go amd64 and arm64 values; realpath uses canonicalize off Linux (Go realpath_other.go); unix-only std calls are behind cfg(unix). a83b66339 (R137 follow-up 3): worker() accepts GOPORT_WORKER_FD only when getppid() equals GOPORT_LAUNCHER_PID, decided once at the start of main, and launch, end_with_launcher and exit use it; the launcher makes the pipe close-on-exec and clears the flag only on the write end, so the worker no longer gets the read end (its write end stays inherited, because no safe call sets the flag on an fd number); new test tests/tsgo_launch.rs. 851ca312c: the LIMIT_SHARE comment gives the measured --checkers 48 exit 70 at ulimit -v 1G. d14ba56e3: lib_parse.bin regenerated after the merges (stored keys only); lib_bind.bin unchanged.

batch.hypothesis: Five gap audit fixes and the R137 worker hardening close gaps with Go, and emit and check output on query, hono, zod and effect stays byte-equal to R137. (1) pjcache: multi-threaded -p --incremental writes Go's packageJsons and missingPackageJsons lists, the same in each run. (2) sortfix: each ported Go sort site uses the Go sort that it ports, so a comparator that is not a total order (compareSymbols) cannot panic, and the vscode imports codeAction and completion panics stop. (3) stacks: thread stacks and glibc arenas follow RLIMIT_AS and RLIMIT_DATA, so query check and emit give Go's output under ulimit -v 2G to 8G, where R137 exits 70; with no limit nothing changes. (4) identity: a build-time version and a port of Go's noembed build let a release build match shipped tsc 7.0.2, and the default build is unchanged. (5) platforms1: cfg gates let ts_goport pass cargo check for darwin, windows and arm64 Linux, and fswatch uses the target's open flags on arm64 Linux. (6) R137 follow-up 3: a tsgo is a worker only when its parent is the launcher, so a tsgo started from a worker runs as a plain tsgo and is not killed. R137 follow-up 2: the tsgo CLI audit gives the same results at GOPORT_LAUNCH=1, GOPORT_LAUNCH=0 and Go.

apisess1 decisions and known limits (R151 reviewer item 4): R14: the --async API handles requests one at a time in order; Go N handles each in its own goroutine, so pipelined dependent requests can differ (Go itself fails them with snapshot not found in 10 of 10 runs). Known limits, same as R149 or Go: a client callback with no answer blocks LSP shutdown (followups1 works on it), one extra stderr line at stdin EOF while a callback waits, a second API session blocks the first. No protected test pins the L11 fix yet.
